name: Thymic Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Thymic Epithelial Tumors

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of malignant epithelial cells with cytologic atypia and invasive growth
Radiologic evidence of anterior mediastinal mass with invasive features on CT or MRI
Positive immunohistochemical staining for cytokeratins and CD5 expression
Exclusion of metastatic carcinoma from other primary sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation combined with imaging evidence of invasive anterior mediastinal mass and immunohistochemical profile consistent with thymic carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary correlation including pathology, radiology, and clinical findings.

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in advanced disease
Anemia in cases with paraneoplastic pure red cell aplasia
imaging: CT scan showing anterior mediastinal mass with invasive features
genetic: Frequent mutations in TP53 and CDKN2A genes
Chromosomal abnormalities including gains in chromosome 1q
other: Histopathology showing squamous differentiation or undifferentiated carcinoma
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin, CD5, and CD117

distinguishingFeatures: Less cytologic atypia and less aggressive behavior
More frequent association with myasthenia gravis
Lymphoid cell origin with different histology
Positive markers for lymphoid lineage (e.g., CD20, CD3)

redFlags: Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
Neuromuscular symptoms suggestive of paraneoplastic syndromes
references: Travis WD et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Lung, Pleura, Thymus and Heart. IARC; 2021.
Kondo K, Monden Y. Therapy for thymic epithelial tumors: a clinical study of 1,320 patients from Japan. Ann Thorac Surg. 2003.
Engels EA. Epidemiology of thymoma and associated malignancies. J Thorac Oncol. 2010.
